solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of mouth involved in a quiet falsetto?

indicators.note: something involved is intricate and tangled, so the letters that follow are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer's high falsetto seems to be produced by some part of the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the definition has some truth to it: the soft palate does shape a falsetto note. P for quiet comes from music scores.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft palate is the fleshy rear section of the roof of the mouth, behind the hard bony palate.

clue.text: Ox that brings up young

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up lifts it from bottom to top, so its letters read backwards

blocks.note: tots are young children

explanation.surface: An ox that raises the young of the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings up' looks like child-rearing, which fits the young, but it is the instruction to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stot is an old Scottish and northern dialect word for a young bullock or steer, i.e. a castrated bovine.

clue.text: Joint where gang takes in film

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a flock is a crowd or group
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A dive bar where a gang of hoodlums watches a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a seedy venue for the gang, but it is the anatomical sense. ET is the crossword's favourite film.
explanation.definitionFit: The fetlock is the jointed projection on a horse's leg just above the hoof, where tufts of hair grow.

clue.text: Obstinacy characteristic of Animal Farm?

blocks.note: the plain meaning: stubborn refusal to change one's mind
in Orwell's novel Animal Farm the farm is run by the swine, so its leadership is literally porcine at the top

explanation.surface: Stubbornness as the defining trait of Orwell's farmyard revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: In Animal Farm the pigs Napoleon and Snowball take charge, so the farm is headed by pigs; the question mark flags the pun on the everyday word for stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obstinately stubborn is described idiomatically with this word, which literally suggests a creature's skull on a person.

clue.text: Before university, acquire a coach

indicators.note: one thing placed before another sits ahead of it, so the pieces are set side by side in that order

blocks.note: to land a job is to acquire it
taken as written
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Advice to take on a sports coach or tutor before going to college.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards to the answer: 'university' comes first in the clue but last in the word, because 'Before' places the other pieces ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, a type of coach.

clue.text: Prepare to run: go, dog!

blocks.note: a go in a game is your turn
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: An owner at the park telling a greyhound to get set and then sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' and 'dog' read as a command to a pet, but 'go' is a noun (a turn) and 'dog' is a verb meaning to shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to swing round before fleeing, so it is the moment of readiness to flee from danger.

clue.text: Announced very full agreement

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a very full room is packed, which sounds identical

explanation.surface: A proclamation that everyone is in complete accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very full agreement' reads as total consensus, but 'very full' is the phrase to be sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or deal between parties, so it is a synonym for an agreement.

clue.text: A row about meal taken regularly in drawing room

indicators.note: taking something at regular intervals means every other letter is used
about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written
a tier is a row of seats
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An argument over dinner that keeps breaking out in the drawing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of seats. 'Drawing room' is not a parlour but literally a room for drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's studio or workshop, a place where painters and draughtsmen sketch and work.

clue.text: Play time theme: pets to be groomed

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playtime activity for children: grooming the family pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play time' looks like a single idea, a children's break, but 'Play' is the definition and 'time' is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance about Prospero on his island is one of his best-known stage dramas.

clue.text: Commander with name badge attached in a particular shape

blocks.note: OC is Officer Commanding
a name tag is a badge
a thing stuck on is attached

explanation.surface: An officer wearing an identity badge cut into some distinctive shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply strings the pieces together. OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a specific geometric figure with eight sides, so it is one example of a particular outline.

clue.text: Spell to remember vividly, full of energy

indicators.note: something full of a substance holds it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to relive an event is to recall it as if it were happening again
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An incantation that brings back memories in vivid, energetic detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like magic or spelling, but it is the verb meaning to take over a shift from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell a colleague is to take a turn in their place so they can rest, which is what a replacement worker does.

clue.text: In ground speed test overlapping title-holders

indicators.note: things that overlap share a stretch, so a letter common to both is written only once

blocks.note: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London
tempo is speed or pace
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: At a sports venue, a speed trial runs over into the time set for the champions.
explanation.walkthrough: The O ending one word is the O starting the next, so it appears once. Lord's is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The lords temporal are the hereditary and life peers in the House of Lords, all of whom bear noble rank.

clue.text: Old Presbyterian binding witches to stake with a bit of rope

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
an ante is a poker stake
its first letter

explanation.surface: A stern Calvinist tying witches to the stake for burning with rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The witch-burning picture makes 'stake' a post, but it is a gambling bet. The Covenanters were 17th-century Scots who signed a binding covenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Covenanters were Scottish Presbyterians of the 1600s who pledged themselves to defend their church against royal interference.

clue.text: Daughter abandons dreadful passion

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: A daughter walks away from a terrible love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passion' suggests love, but here it means a fit of strong feeling, specifically rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger or wrath, and passion can mean an outburst of intense emotion such as fury.

clue.text: Appoint criminal to study prison

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or wrong, so the letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
to con a text is to study it closely

explanation.surface: An instruction to assign a lawbreaker to examine the jail system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' also means a convict, which the prison surface pushes; here it is the old verb to study.
explanation.definitionFit: Bentham's panopticon was a circular jail design letting a single guard observe every inmate's cell.

clue.text: Art of self-defence gives splendid child a rounded character

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as I
a kid is a child
O is the round letter

explanation.surface: Martial arts training turns a fine youngster into a well-rounded person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounded character' reads as a balanced personality, but it is the circular letter. A1 (first class) becomes AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial discipline that uses an attacker's momentum against them rather than striking.

clue.text: Announces journey — it starts from here?

blocks.note: to air a view is to announce it
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone declares an expedition and says this is the starting point.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: 'it' is the journey, and a flight begins on the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft take off, so a flight begins its travel from that place.

clue.text: Wears kit adapted: one way to follow a boat

definitions.text: one way to follow a boat

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters are changed into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone puts on specially altered gear to trail behind a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: skiing on water behind a speedboat is literally a way of following it.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-skiers are towed on a rope behind a motorboat, gliding across its wake on skis.

clue.text: Rock band so bad I must repeatedly interrupt

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
to interrupt is to break in, and doing it more than once means breaking in at two places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, used twice

explanation.surface: A heckler complains that a rock group is terrible and keeps butting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock band' reads as a music group, but 'Rock' is the definition and 'band' is anagram fodder; the single letter I goes in twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a dark glassy volcanic stone formed when lava cools very quickly, so it is a type of rock.

clue.text: Love to drill through card to find pistol

indicators.note: drilling through something bores into its middle, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: a SIM card sits in a mobile phone
dear and love are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Someone happily bores into a card and discovers a gun hidden inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as zero is the usual crossword reflex, but here it is an endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a weapon worn at the belt or hip, typically a handgun or revolver.

clue.text: Broken fragments presenting girl with no end of danger

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a deb (debutante) is a young society woman
risk means danger

explanation.surface: Shattered pieces pose a hazard to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A deb is a debutante, a girl making her formal entry into high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered rubble and pieces left after something has been smashed or destroyed.

clue.text: Debauched man saves money for habit

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it stored away, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: a roué is a dissolute rake
tin is old British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A dissolute man puts money aside to fund his vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' in the surface is a drug or drink habit; the definition is the everyday sense of a regular practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed sequence of actions performed regularly, just as a habit is a settled regular practice.

clue.text: Hurry away and keep busy

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang command to leave quickly
second meaning, read as three words: to remain hard at work

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the letters split differently, as BE AT IT, which ignores the enumeration's word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for scram or clear off matches leaving fast, and being at it means staying occupied with work.

clue.text: A little information should come back shortly

indicators.note: shortly here means in a shortened form, so the word loses its last letter
coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: data is information

explanation.surface: A small piece of news ought to be returned to you soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' reads as 'soon' but means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a small amount, used as a noun or adverbially, as in 'a tad salty'.

clue.text: Sum not completed in crucial test

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a sum with a number followed by a plus sign and nothing after it is unfinished
second meaning: a British exam deciding a child's secondary school

explanation.walkthrough: The eleven-plus is an exam taken by some British children at about eleven to decide entry to selective grammar schools, so it was a crucial test.
explanation.definitionFit: The exam is named after the pupils' age, and written as an arithmetic phrase it is a calculation missing its second term.

clue.text: Watery liquid from height dropping into uprooted tree

indicators.note: something pulled up by the roots is turned over, so in a down entry it reads upwards
dropping into something means falling inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the yew is an evergreen tree
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Sap falling from a great height into a toppled tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Whey is what Little Miss Muffet ate with her curds.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the thin watery part of milk that separates from the curds when cheese is made.

clue.text: Girl fills reverse of dry forms

indicators.note: the reverse of something is its back-to-front version, so the letters are read the other way
to fill something is to occupy its inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: sec is the French wine term for dry
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman completes the back pages of some tedious official paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' suggests paperwork, but in British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools, pupils are grouped into forms, the traditional name for classes of the same year.

clue.text: Dull, like a mountain lake?

blocks.note: a tarn is a small upland lake
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: Describing something as grey and flat as a lake up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order, 'like' first; the question mark flags the jokey coinage of a lake-ish word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to make a metal surface lose its shine, which is to dull or discolour it.

clue.text: Dead queen ignored by count

indicators.note: something ignored is left out of consideration, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
to number things is to count them

explanation.surface: A late monarch snubbed by a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a European noble snubbing royalty, but it is the verb to count.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone dead has lost all sensation, which is exactly what being without feeling means.

clue.text: Amateur work involves quieter, spirited works?

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: DIY is do-it-yourself home improvement
stiller means calmer or more hushed

explanation.surface: Home handiwork turns out calmer yet livelier productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' means a factory, and 'spirited' refers to the whisky or gin made there, not to liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery is a plant producing alcoholic spirits, so it is a factory whose output is spirits.
